alternate_names: Sri Chaturmukha Brahma Lingeshwara Swamy Temple
deities: Chaturmukha Brahma Lingeshwara (Shiva Lingam with four faces of Brahma carved on it)

history.dynasty: Vasireddy (present structure, 1783-1816); earlier Chola, Eastern Chalukya, Pallava and Kakatiya contributions
history.period: Site 10th-14th century origins; present temple rebuilt late 18th - early 19th century (approx. 200 years old)
history.summary: The Chaturmukha Brahma Temple stands in Chebrolu, an ancient temple town (once called Chatturmukhapuram, Sambhole and Tambrapuri) whose inscriptions credit 101 shrines to Chola, Eastern Chalukya, Pallava and Kakatiya patronage. Its presiding deity is a Shiva Lingam with the four faces of Lord Brahma carved on its four sides — Chaturmukha (four-faced) Brahma Lingeshwara — worshipping Brahma alongside Shiva. The legend behind this rare Brahma shrine is that the sage Bhrugu cursed Brahma to have no worship on earth in Kaliyuga, so no separate idol of Brahma was consecrated; instead his four faces, symbolising the four Vedas and the four directions, were engraved on the lingam. The temple stands in the middle of a tank, reached by a bridge, surrounded by two small Shiva shrines (east and west), two Vishnu shrines (north and south) and four Shakti shrines at the corners; a Nandi carved from a single red stone stands outside. The present structure was rebuilt about 200 years ago by Raja Vasireddy Venkatadri Naidu (1783-1816), who legend says built temples as penance after killing robbers who terrorised the region.

name: Chaturmukha Brahma Temple
town_description: Amaravati, the location in the source list, is the planned capital city of Andhra Pradesh on the banks of the Krishna River, developed around the ancient Buddhist heritage zone of Dharanikota/Amaravati — once a Satavahana capital famed for its great stupa — and the adjacent temple town of Amaravathi, home to the Amareswara Pancharama temple. The Chaturmukha Brahma Temple itself stands about 45 km away in Chebrolu, an old temple town near Guntur with a dense cluster of historic shrines.

travel.airport: Vijayawada International Airport (approx. 63 km; taxis and cabs available).
travel.railway: Guntur Junction (approx. 16 km), well connected across Andhra Pradesh and beyond.
travel.road: Chebrolu is easily reachable from Guntur (approx. 16 km) by bus and autorickshaw; the temple is on Patha Reddy Palem Road, Chebrolu 522212, roughly 45 km from Amaravati town.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March (pleasant season); Karthika Pournami (October-November) and Maha Shivaratri (February-March) are the main festival days.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Morning 6:00 AM to 12:00 noon; evening 4:00 PM to 8:00 PM (verify — one source lists a single 6:00 AM to 8:00 PM window). Address: Chebrolu, Chebrolu Mandal, Guntur district 522212.
